title: Not 5 but 6! Cartesian Product Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
The college canteen sells three snacks and two drinks. Most people guess five combos, but there are six, and one more drink makes it nine. Why do choices multiply instead of add? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 2, Relations and Functions) we open the new chapter with its first idea: the Cartesian product of two sets.

You will watch every snack pair with every drink on an arrow diagram, see the same six combos as dots on a grid, and add drinks live while the count grows three at a time. Then the NCERT definition of A × B, a four-step proof of n(A × B) = n(A) · n(B), union versus product side by side, a pause-and-think on the empty set, a worked example with set builder form, the exam trap of pairing like a zip, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 3 snacks, 2 drinks: why 6 combos?
0:29 Build every combo: the arrow diagram
0:54 Live: add a drink, watch the grid grow
1:23 Definition: the Cartesian product A × B
1:52 Proof: n(A × B) = n(A) · n(B)
2:34 Union adds, product multiplies
2:51 Pause and think: an empty set
3:17 Worked example: A × B in roster form
4:02 Exam trap: pairing like a zip
4:19 Where it is asked
4:29 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:10 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 14): Ordered Pairs. Exam hall seat (3, 5) is not seat (5, 3). Why does the order change everything?

Video by Quest Academy.
